title: AlloyDB tools return "Tool ... not found" even after AlloyDB is READY
problem_statement: /database/info?db=alloydb and any alloydb_* tool call return {"error":"Tool 'alloydb_describe_database' not found."}, persisting even after the AlloyDB instance reaches READY state (confirmed not a startup-timing issue).
root_cause: database.tf's metadata_startup_script bakes tools_db/tools.yaml into the Oracle VM via Terraform's file() interpolation and rewrites it on every boot, but its sed substitution block only resolves ${ORACLE_*} placeholders -- it never adds the five ${ALLOYDB_HOST}/${ALLOYDB_PORT}/${ALLOYDB_DATABASE}/${ALLOYDB_USER}/${ALLOYDB_PASSWORD} lines. Toolbox loads the file with those placeholders still literal, so the alloydb-db source block (and every tool depending on it, including alloydb_describe_database) silently fails to register -- Oracle tools load fine, masking the gap.
solution_steps: Confirm it is not a timing issue: check gcloud alloydb instances list shows STATUS=READY, then re-curl -- if the error persists, it is the sed gap, not startup lag.

Temporary fix (safe, no Terraform apply): build a fully-resolved tools.yaml locally with BOTH Oracle and AlloyDB placeholders substituted, gcloud compute scp it to the VM, then docker restart toolbox -- confirm via logs it reports the full tool count (e.g. 'Initialized 19 tools') including alloydb_describe_database.

This temporary fix lives only on the VM disk and silently reverts on the next Oracle VM stop/start or reboot, since the startup script unconditionally overwrites tools.yaml from stale Terraform-baked metadata every boot -- re-apply after every restart until the permanent fix ships.

Permanent fix: add the 5 missing ${ALLOYDB_*} sed -e lines to database.tf's metadata_startup_script and apply deliberately with a VM snapshot first -- changing metadata_startup_script forces full VM replacement, so this must never go through a rushed terraform apply.
